title: Collections & objects — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: This is one of the largest surfaces in the library: ~155 list operations in a 6,500-line Zig core behind a 1,600-method Ring face, a functional pipeline, deep-path search, Lodash-grade grouping, and a reflective object root that 449 classes inherit. It is tuned for millions of items with measured residency wins. Two honest limits keep it short of the very top: boxed value storage holds raw set-op throughput an order of magnitude below NumPy/native, there are no persistent immutable structures, and the legacy test grind is mid-flight — so the ratings lean on the narrated and engine suites that pass.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. The core operations are engine-backed and guarded by the narrated suites; the caveats are about scale ceilings, immutability, and the fidelity grind noted below.

lanes.engine: Index, slice, section, insert, remove, reverse, swap, rotate, repeat — the full vocabulary, reads and reverse engine-backed via `stz_list_get/slice/reverse/rotate`. Mutators route through Ring submodules (`stzListInserter/Remover/Mover`) then re-cache.
lanes.owed: Comprehensive and correct. The only structural note is that mutators still make a Ring hop before invalidating the engine cache — a residency detail, not a capability gap.

lanes.engine: Engine-backed `map_expr` / `filter_expr` / `reduce_expr` using a string DSL (`@item`, `@accumulator`), plus two predicate modes: `W` (string-expression, engine) and `WF` (Ring function, in-VM) across Find/Filter/Count/Positions/Remove/Replace.
lanes.owed: A real, dual-mode functional surface. The string-expression path even runs the predicate in the engine, which the peers cannot do — a genuine differentiator.

lanes.engine: The full finder family engine-backed (`find_cs`, `find_all_cs`, `find_nth_cs`, `contains_cs`, `starts/ends_with`) plus a deep-path API (`deep_find`, `item_at_path`, `paths_at_depth`) that Lodash-style `get` only approximates.
lanes.owed: Cross-module needle handles are already solved (`find_all_held_cs`). Nothing structural owed on the search lane.

lanes.engine: Union, intersection, difference, subset, unique — all engine-backed (`stz_list_union_cs` etc.) with a scalar `splitmix64` fast path for int/float keys (1M int-union ~43% faster).
lanes.owed: A footgun to know: `intersection_cs` dedups (true set) while `common_items_cs` keeps left order and duplicates (multiset). And boxed storage keeps 1M int-union at ~2–3s vs Python's ~0.1s — the unboxed frontier (lane 9).

lanes.engine: Full Lodash-grade reshaping, engine-backed: `classify_cs`, `partition`, `chunked`, `split_to_parts_of_n`, `zip`, `interleave`, `sliding_window`, `frequencies_cs` — `classify` even emits the final nested shape engine-side (−51% at 1M).
lanes.owed: Broad and fast. A window / stream abstraction that returns lazily (rather than materialising) would be the only refinement worth naming.

lanes.engine: `sort`, `sort_cs`, `sort_descending`, `sort_by_expr` (key expression), `sort_on`, `sorted_insert`, and a full predicate set (`is_sorted`, `is_strictly_increasing`, `is_monotonic`) — all engine-backed.
lanes.owed: At parity, with a case-sensitivity dial and key-expression sorting the peers match but rarely improve on.

lanes.engine: Stats built into the collection, engine-backed: `sum`, `product`, `mean`, `median`, `variance`, `stddev`, `nth_largest`, `ranked` — also surfaced on `stzListOfNumbers`.
lanes.owed: A useful bonus on a collection, but the deep statistical story (distributions, tests, the careful compensated summation) lives on the Statistics page — rated Solid here as a convenience lane.

lanes.engine: Ring assigns lists by value — copy-on-assign and copy-on-return — which gives safety by default (no accidental aliasing) and a clean `Copy()`. The residency layer works with this rather than against it.
lanes.owed: No persistent immutable structures with structural sharing: a "modified copy" of a large list is a full copy, not an O(log n) share. The whole residency effort (lane 9) exists to soften exactly this cost.

lanes.engine: A measured residency system: a bounded, generation-keyed cache (FIFO eviction at 8M items / 1024 entries, so the 8192-slot handle table never overflows) plus copy-elimination on unmarshal. Measured: read-reuse 3.34s→1.29s (2.6×), Classify −51%, Union −34% at 1M items.
lanes.owed: Items are boxed `*StzValue`, so native-speed set-ops need unboxed typed storage (deferred). And the migration is half-done: Slice 4 (engine-truth) and Slice 5 (submodule residency) are open, with ~32 marshal-in sites remaining.

lanes.engine: One reflective root inherited by 449 classes: introspection (`Attributes`, `Methods`, `Type`, `ObjectUID`), comparison, cloning, Q-elevation (`Q(...)` lifts a raw value into a chainable object), and the function-form grammar — `Verb()` mutates, `Verbed()` copies, `VerbQ()` chains.
lanes.owed: The root's own `#TODO` notes the common surface is not fully abstracted — some behaviour is duplicated across children for semantic reasons. A consolidation, not a capability gap.

lanes.engine: A wide family: `stzHashList` / associative list, `stzGrid`, `stzTree`, `stzSet`, `stzListOfLists` / 2D, `stzListOfPairs`, `stzListOfSections`, `stzYielder` — the structured-collection catalogue.
lanes.owed: Most of this family is Ring-side (not scale-tuned), and `stzHashList` folds keys to lowercase and is not a true hash map — a documented trap. Rich, but shallower than the core list under the engine.

lanes.engine: `stzListNamedParams` — a 1,945-method grammar for natural-language named arguments (`IsOnSection`, `IsHarvest`, `IsYield…NamedParam`) that lets call sites read close to English. A distinctive Softanza mechanism with no direct peer.
lanes.owed: Pure Ring, and its correctness under the fidelity grind (lane note below) is the least-verified of the group. A powerful, distinctive surface carrying real coverage debt.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first pays down the coverage debt the ratings depend on and lifts the one hard performance ceiling; the second finishes measured work already in flight; the third is the strategic reach toward Immutable.js and a real map.

items.title: Finish the list narration / fidelity grind
items.text: About 312 of ~602 legacy test blocks error — mostly R14 "method without definition" from renamed aliases — and the fidelity marker pass is uncaptured. The core is proven by the narrated and engine suites, but closing this turns the whole advertised surface from claimed into guarded.

items.title: Unboxed typed storage for native-speed set-ops
items.text: Items are boxed `*StzValue`, so a 1M int-union runs ~2–3s against Python's ~0.1s. Typed unboxed arrays for scalar lists would close the last order-of-magnitude gap — the deliberately-deferred frontier.

tiers.title: Tier B — finish work already in flight

items.title: Complete the residency migration
items.text: Slice 4 (engine-truth / lazy `@aContent`) and Slice 5 (submodule residency) with the ~32 remaining marshal-in sites. The infrastructure and measurements exist; this is finishing a measured win, not starting one.

items.title: Disambiguate the set-op semantics
items.text: Make the set-vs-multiset choice explicit at the API so `intersection_cs` (dedups) and `common_items_cs` (keeps order + duplicates) can't be confused silently — a naming/doc fix over correct engine code.

items.title: Consolidate the object root
items.text: Act on `stzObject`'s own `#TODO`: abstract the common behaviour duplicated across children. Reduces surface area and drift across 449 classes.

items.title: Persistent immutable collections
items.text: Structural-sharing lists/maps so a "modified copy" is O(log n), not a full copy — the Immutable.js / Clojure lane. It would also relieve the pressure the residency system was built to absorb.

items.title: A true hash map for stzHashList
items.text: Real key semantics — case-preserving, arbitrary key types — instead of the current lowercase-folding associative list. Lifts the specialized-collections lane toward Python `dict` / Immutable.js `Map`.

items.title: Lazy / streaming pipeline
items.text: A lazy iterator that fuses map/filter/take without materialising intermediates — the one thing Rust iterators and Lodash chains do that the engine-expr pipeline does not yet.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: The core is proven: `00_list_narrated` (79 assertions), the large-scale guards, and ~30 `test_*` engine/delegation checkers all pass. But the ~602-file legacy suite is mid-grind — 312 blocks error, dominated by renamed-method calls, and the object module carries a stale expectation (`HowManyStzClasses()=60` when 449+ classes now inherit the root). The lane ratings describe the engine-backed capability the trustworthy suites exercise, not the full alias surface that grind will reconcile.

Softanza's collections are broader and more engine-backed than any single stdlib or Lodash — a functional pipeline, deep search, Lodash-grade grouping and a reflective object root, tuned for millions — and its distance from the very top is two specific things: boxed storage (vs NumPy-native throughput) and the absence of persistent immutable structures (vs Immutable.js).
